design_repair.name: full_sample_unpenalized_logistic_mle
design_repair.rationale: The V9 cross-fitted regularized propensity retained material post-weighting imbalance in age, diagnosis year, and W_T_missing within the restricted V10 cohort. Before any V10 effect was computed, the propensity nuisance is changed to a low-dimensional unpenalized logistic maximum-likelihood model over the same 13 baseline variables. Censoring and outcome nuisances remain cross-fitted exactly as in Candidate V9.
design_repair.imputation: full-cohort median for each baseline feature
design_repair.scaling: full-cohort mean zero and unit population SD
design_repair.zero_variance_columns: excluded from fitting but retained in balance tables

locked_estimator.treatment: Hormone therapy initiated during days 0-180 versus no initiation by day 180.
locked_estimator.propensity: Full-sample unpenalized logistic MLE on the locked 13-variable compact baseline set, refitted in every patient-bootstrap sample.
locked_estimator.censoring: Exact Candidate V9 cross-fitted discrete-time regularized logistic censoring model.
locked_estimator.outcome_regression: Exact Candidate V9 cross-fitted arm-specific bounded RidgeCV model on the IPCW-RMST pseudo-outcome.
locked_estimator.score: Exact Candidate V9 ATO-AIPW score except for the locked propensity nuisance change.
locked_estimator.primary_sensitivity: Original Candidate V9 cross-fitted regularized propensity applied to the same locked V10 population.

disclosure: Post hoc design-stage amendment. Candidate V9 identified the need for a chemotherapy-sequencing audit. Stage 25 then froze the strict V10 population but failed the prespecified weighted-balance gate. Candidate V10 treatment effects remained uncomputed. Stage 25B revises only the propensity nuisance using treatment and baseline covariates, then locks the design before effect estimation.
